**Transformer Construction & Comparison:**
* **Core Type:** Windings surround a considerable part of the core. It has a single magnetic circuit. Used for high voltage, low kVA ratings.
* **Shell Type:** Core surrounds a considerable part of the windings. It has a double magnetic circuit. Used for low voltage, high kVA ratings.

| Feature | Core Type | Shell Type |
|---|---|---|
| Magnetic path | Single | Double |
| Mechanical support | Less robust | More robust |
| Cooling | Better natural cooling | Requires careful cooling design |

**Numerical Calculation:**
Given: $P_{rated} = 40\text{ kVA}$, Iron loss $P_i = 800\text{ W}$, Full load copper loss $P_{cu} = 1140\text{ W}$.

*(i) Efficiency at full load, unity power factor ($\cos\phi = 1$):*
$$\text{Output} = 40 \times 10^3 \times 1 = 40,000\text{ W}$$
$$\text{Total Losses} = P_i + P_{cu} = 800 + 1140 = 1940\text{ W}$$
$$\eta_{FL} = \frac{40000}{40000 + 1940} \times 100 = 95.38\%$$

*(ii) Efficiency at half load, $0.8$ pf lagging:*
$$\text{Output} = \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 40,000\right) \times 0.8 = 16,000\text{ W}$$
$$\text{Copper loss at half load} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 \times P_{cu} = 0.25 \times 1140 = 285\text{ W}$$
$$\text{Total Losses} = P_i + P_{cu(half)} = 800 + 285 = 1085\text{ W}$$
$$\eta_{HL} = \frac{16000}{16000 + 1085} \times 100 = 93.65\% $$
proTip: Copper loss varies directly as the square of the load fraction ($x^2 \times P_{cu}$), whereas iron loss remains constant.
